OVER 40 BRANCHES
CAPITAL $6,000,000 MEX.

March 4, 1929.

Criminal Intelligence Department,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Hankow Road, Shanghai.

Dear Sirs:

Our attention has recently been called to a paper
entitled "Chinese Record" containing radical propaganda and
being falsely circulated in brown paper wrapper bearing the
address of our company and that of Edward Evans as the senders.
The paper is published in English.

We wish to inform you that it is absolutely against
the policy of our company to publish, print, sell, or handle the
paper of this kind. We shall appreciate if you will investigate
into this matter and take proper actions to prevent the re-
occurrence of such an affair.

Yours truly,
THE COMMERCIAL PRESS. LTD.
SALES OFFICE, SHANGHAI

敬启者：

我方近期注意到一份名为《中国记录》（Chinese Record）的刊物，其中含有激进宣传内容，且被虚假地装在印有我方公司地址及爱德华·埃文斯（Edward Evans）作为寄件人的牛皮纸包装中流通。该刊物以英文出版。

我方谨此告知，出版、印刷、销售或经手此类刊物完全违背我方公司政策。如蒙贵方调查此事并采取适当措施以防止此类事件再次发生，我方将不胜感激。

此致
敬礼

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
File No. D. 73......
Date....3..5..29...

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
May 1, 1929.

Communistic literature in wrappers
bearing name of one or other of
the more prominent printing houses book-sellers

There have been brought to my notice during the past two
months cases where communistic publications entitled "The
China Herald" (printed in English), "The Chinese Record"
(in English and also an abridged Chinese edition) and
"Progressive China" (in both Chinese and English) have been
sent through the Post Office in wrappers bearing the name and
address of one or other of the more prominent Shanghai
book-selling printing establishments (such as Edward Evans & Son, The
Chinese-American Publishing Company and the Commercial
Press), obviously with a view to evading the censors.

Investigation in conjunction with the Chinese Authorities
has so far been without result.

(批：China Herald not checked 3.5.29.)

Copies of the "China Herald" and "The Chinese Record"
(English and Chinese) are attached to this file and I am
endeavouring to secure a copy of "Progressive China."

(批：Type 5 copies for)

I attach draft reply to the American Consul-General.

Thos Rubinstein
C. D. I.

A/D.C.I.

(刑事侦缉处) 办公笔记
1929年5月1日。

共产主义文献装在印有
某家较著名印刷厂或书商之名的包装纸中

在过去两个月里，我注意到多起案件，涉及题为《中国先驱报》（The China Herald，英文印刷）、《中国记录》（The Chinese Record，英文版及中文缩编版）和《进步中国》（Progressive China，中英文版）的共产主义出版物，这些刊物通过邮局寄送，包装纸上印有上海某家较著名的售书印刷机构（如爱德华·埃文斯父子书店 Edward Evans & Son、中美出版公司 The Chinese-American Publishing Company 和商务印书馆 The Commercial Press）的名称和地址，显然是为了逃避审查。

与中国当局联合进行的调查迄今尚无结果。

（批注：《中国先驱报》未核查 1929年5月3日。）

《中国先驱报》和《中国记录》（中英文版）的副本已附于本档案中，我正努力获取《进步中国》的副本。

（批注：打字5份供）

我附上给美国总领事的回复草稿。

Thos Rubinstein
C. D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 73
Date 3. 5. 29

May 1, 29.

Sir,

The use of names of foreigners for the
issuance of Communist propaganda.

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of
your letter No. 800 E/CCC of April 22 on the above
subject and in reply to state that several cases
have recently come to the notice of the Shanghai
Municipal Police where communistic publications
entitled "The China Herald", "The Chinese Record"
and "Progressive China" have been sent through the
Post Office in wrappers bearing the name and address
of one or other of the more prominent Shanghai book-
selling establishments, obviously with a view to
evading the censors.

I regret however that investigation by the
Municipal Police and the Chinese Authorities with
view to locating the source of those publications
has so far been without result.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Acting Commissioner of Police.

E. S. Cunningham, Esq.,
American Consul-General,
Shanghai.

1929年5月1日。

先生：

关于利用外国人姓名发行共产主义宣传品一事。

谨此确认收到阁下4月22日关于上述主题的第800 E/CCC号来信，并回复如下：上海公共租界警务处近期注意到多起案件，涉及题为《中国先驱报》、《中国记录》和《进步中国》的共产主义出版物，这些刊物通过邮局寄送，包装纸上印有上海某家较著名售书机构的名称和地址，显然是为了逃避审查。

然而，遗憾的是，警务处与中国当局为查明这些出版物来源而进行的调查迄今尚无结果。

此致
敬礼

您的恭顺仆人，

代理警务处处长。

E. S. Cunningham 先生，
美国总领事，
上海。

C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. 1: Q. D.. 73
Date.. 25. 4. 29

AMERICAN CONSULAR SERVICE
American Consulate General
Shanghai, China, April 22, 1929.

Subject: The use of names of foreigners
for the issuance of Communist
propaganda.

Captain E. I. M. Barrett, C.I.P.;
Commissioner of Police,
18 Hankow Road, Shanghai.

Sir:

There have been at least two issues of a periodical
entitled "Progressive China" published in both the Chinese
and English language mailed to various residences in China
for the month of March under a label bearing an imprint
which would lead one to believe it was the imprint of The
Chinese-American Publishing Company, 25 Nanking Road.

I have the honor to make inquiry as to any information
the police authorities may have concerning the persons re-
sponsible for this magazine.

I have the honor to be, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Edwin S. Cunningham,
American Consul General.

800 B/02Q
ESC/EW

No. L. O. D..73....
Date....9.4.29...

April 9,

Sir,

"The China Record"

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of
your Special Branch 1212/1929 and in reply to state
that several cases have recently come to the notice
of the Shanghai Municipal Police where the above
publication has been sent through the Post Office
in a wrapper bearing the name and address of one or
other of the most prominent Shanghai printing
establishments, obviously with a view to evading
the censors. The American Book Company, 24 Nanking
Road, is a firm of repute and entirely above suspicion.
So far nothing is known of the Chinese Aid
Society which would appear to be responsible for the
offending publication.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,

J A Director of Criminal Investigation.

Director of Criminal Intelligence,
Straits Settlements,
Singapore.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. REGISTRY
No. L. C. 15. 73......
5. 4. 29......

Extract from "Police Journal, Straits Settlements" dated
March 15, 1929.

From documents discovered in Singapore there is
reason to believe that the local communist party, either on
instructions or as a result of propaganda received from
China, will attempt the formation of Aid Societies. A
bound pamphlet printed in good English and posted in Shanghai
apparently by the American Book Company, entitled "The Chinese
Aid Society" (volume 1, No. 1) has been found in Singapore.
This contains purely communist propaganda. Certain documents
recently found by the Police in connection with the arrest of
TAN PEK HAI deal with the organisation of Aid societies.

One document -- a circular letter from the Kwang-
tung Headquarters of China's Aid Society -- is addressed to
compatriots in the South Seas and is dated 25th January, 1929.
While professing to be entirely non-party, it is in tone
strongly anti-Kuomintang, anti-capitalist and pro-labour.
A second document dated 29th January, 1929, is published
locally by the South Seas Provisional Committee of the Communist
Party and is entitled "Notification No. 53 concerning the work-
ings of the Aid Society."

It is based obviously on the circular letter mentioned
above and contains full instructions as to the formation of
such an organisation describing the methods by which the
apparently innocuous and humanitarian Aid Society will embody
a strong communist element whose duty it will be to indulge in
subversive movements amongst the working classes.

To S. D. Kay.
add to file please
WHS
4/4/29.

C. I. 登记室
编号 L. C. 15. 73......
1929年 4月 5日......

摘录自1929年3月15日的《海峡殖民地警务杂志》。

从在新加坡发现的文件中有理由相信，当地共产党要么是根据指示，要么是作为收到来自中国宣传的结果，将试图组建援助社。在新加坡发现了一本用良好英文印刷并在上海寄出的装订小册子，显然由美国图书公司寄出，题为《中国援助社》（第1卷，第1期）。其中包含纯粹的共产主义宣传。警方近期在逮捕 TAN PEK HAI（音译）一案中发现的某些文件涉及援助社的组织工作。

其中一份文件——一封来自中国援助社广东总部的通函——是写给南洋同胞的，日期为1929年1月25日。虽然声称完全无党派色彩，但其语气强烈反国民党、反资本主义且亲劳工。第二份文件日期为1929年1月29日，由共产党南洋临时委员会在当地出版，题为“关于援助社运作的第53号通知”。

它显然基于上述通函，并包含关于组建此类组织的完整指示，描述了这种表面上无害且具人道主义色彩的援助社如何体现强烈的共产主义元素，其职责是在工人阶级中进行颠覆活动。

致 S. D. Kay。
请归档
WHS
1929年4月4日。

North China Command.

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
March 12, 1929.

"The China Record"

With reference to letter dated March 5 from Colonel
Halland, I have been in close touch with the Chinese
Authorities who are making exhaustive enquiries with a
view to locating the author or authors of this publication
but so far without result. Nothing is known of the
"Chinese Aid Society" which, from a perusal of the magazine,
would appear to be responsible for its publication.
Attached are two copies of the Chinese publication referred
to in the last paragraph of Mr. Cook's report of March 2.
These were obtained from the Post Office censors and,
like the English publication, are issued by the "Chinese
Aid Society."

I also attach three copies, English version, of the
"China Record" and suggest that two of these be forwarded
to Colonel Halland and the third to Headquarters, North
China Command.

Jhn Rubentam
C. D. I.

A/D.C.I.

《中国记录》

关于 Halland 上校3月5日的来信，我一直与中国当局保持密切联系，他们正在进行详尽查询，以期找到该刊物的作者，但迄今尚无结果。对于“中国援助社”我们一无所知，但从对该杂志的阅读来看，该社似乎应对其出版负责。

我还附上三份《中国记录》的英文版，建议将其中两份转交给 Halland 上校，第三份转交给华北司令部总部。

H. B. M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.
5th. March, 1929.

My dear Aiers,

I understand that Edward Evans &
Sons, Ltd., of 17 Kiukiang Road recently received
copies of a Communist publication entitled the "Chinese

the "White Terror", the Kuomintang and calling for ven-

publication I should be very grateful if you would kindly

formation which you may have collected regarding the
authors of this publication.

Yours sincerely,
C. H. N. Hall

The photographs contained in
the "Chinese Record", attached herewith
were taken by a representative of
the "China Mail" which is published
at Hong Kong by Mr. Burnett the
editor.
The type is 10 point, old-

随函附上的《中国记录》（"Chinese Record"）中所含照片，系由在香港出版该刊物的编辑伯内特（Burnett）先生的一位代表拍摄。
字体为10点大小，混用旧式与新式铅字，且以旧式铅字手工排版。由于铅字短缺，印刷工作是在一家正规印刷厂内分阶段完成的。据本地字体专家认定，这一特定出版物并非在上海印刷，有人推测这可能是韦尔牧师（Rev. Twell）的作品，他在广州沙面（Shambei）拥有一家印刷机构。
另有一份中文刊物，载有相同照片，据称是由莫斯科组织“国际革命战士救济会”（M.O.P.R.，International Society for the relief of prisoners revolutionary）提供资金印刷的。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. Q. D. 73......
Date...........M. 1. 29

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MARCH 1, 1929

COMMUNISTS' NEW
TRICKS

Foreign Firm's Name Used to
Despatch Propaganda
Through Posts

We have been shown a copy of
"The Chinese Record"—not to be
confused with a magazine of an
almost similar name—specified as
Vol. I, No. I, sent through the post
office in a wrapper bearing, in a
rectangle the name and address of
Messrs. Edward Evans & Sons, Ltd.,
with the name of well known Chinese
publishing house on the inside of
the very same wrapper.
The pamphlet is obviously a "red"
production destined to emphasize
what the Chinese communists are
alleged have suffered at the hands
of the "white" Chinese substantiated
with photographs of the outrages
in Canton with which most people
are by now perfectly well acquaint-
ed.
Messrs. Edward Evans & Sons
are in no way responsible either
for the publication of the pamphlet
or its dissemination through the
post. The address given on the
wrapper as that of Messrs. Evans
& Sons was vacated by them more
than two years ago and the whole
"get-up" of the wrapper is that
of an impudent forgery making
use of a valued foreign name for
the purpose of spreading some
particularly obnoxious Communist
propaganda.

（批：Intell. Section,
I understand you are
attending to this matter.
JMS
2/3/29）

（批：a. c (Pol)
HR 1 3/9）

（批：HR）

《字林西报》，1929年3月1日，星期五

共产党人的新花招

利用洋行名义通过邮政寄送宣传品

我们被出示了一份《中国记录》（"The Chinese Record"）——切勿与名称几乎相同的另一本杂志混淆——标明为第一卷第一期，通过邮局寄送，其包装纸上的矩形框内印有爱德华·埃文斯父子有限公司（Messrs. Edward Evans & Sons, Ltd.）的名称和地址，而在同一张包装纸的内侧则印有一家知名中国书局的名称。
这本小册子显然是一份“红色”出版物，旨在强调据称中国共产党员在“白色”中国人手中遭受的苦难，并辅以广州暴行的照片，大多数人对这些暴行如今已十分熟悉。
爱德华·埃文斯父子有限公司对该小册子的出版或通过邮政进行传播均不承担任何责任。包装纸上所列埃文斯父子公司的地址，他们已于两年多前搬离，整个包装的“设计”纯属无耻的伪造，利用受人尊敬的外国商号名称来散布特别令人反感的共产主义宣传。

我知悉你们正在处理此事。
